taxonomyNote: NatureServe places North American treefrogs in Dryophytes (Duellman et al. 2016); ADW and the batch list use Hyla. NatureServe name: Dryophytes squirellus.
fieldMarks: Solid green to brown, sometimes with darker splotches; can change colour with temperature and time of day.
Light stripe (usually yellow, sometimes white or orange) along the upper jaw; stripe larger in males.
Breeding males have a prominent dark green or brown vocal sac.
behavior: Nocturnal, most active just after dusk and before dawn and in rain; in daylight enters torpor.
Gives a 'rain call' from trees and bushes when rain is impending.
Hides under loose bark, palm leaves and tree holes; lays up to about 1,000 eggs in spring or summer.
habitat: Open woods, cities and towns and thick low vegetation near water; breeds in flooded ditches, flatwoods ponds, swamps and stock ponds.
range: Coastal Plain and Mississippi Valley from southern Texas and southern Arkansas to southeastern Virginia and Florida; introduced on Grand Bahama. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Green treefrog
lookalikes.howToTell: Larger with a white or yellowish side stripe running onto the leg.

lookalikes.name: Pine woods treefrog
lookalikes.howToTell: Orange or silver spots on rear thighs; raspy Morse-like call.
